title: Tenor trombone
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS tenor trombone (model and player are stated as NA on the page)
summary: Limits first: the lip is an artificial latex pair (Cullen 2000), not a player's, except that F3 carries the resonances and Q of a human lip measured by Newton (2009) on Cullen's mass (F3 sounds at the measured player's 170 Hz and rises from 8 to 10 of 14, with Copley and Strong's printed forte lip width of 13.4 mm in place of Cullen's 12 mm), and that Bb2 and Eb3, since 2026-11-10, carry lips built from prints and blown at a measured pressure (the Bb2 entry of physics_present: Newton's Q and second mode, a mass derived from Bromage's printed lip opening, a resonance of 78 Hz that is a setting contradicting Newton's printed 55 to 58 Hz, an assumed closed rest gap, Cullen's width and second-mode mass, and 1329 Pa; the page is darker than the one it replaces and counts 12 of 14 against 11; the Eb3 entry gives the same for Eb3, with Q, the second mode and the lip opening interpolated between the Bb2 and F3 prints, a resonance of 99 Hz that is a setting, and 1728 Pa; that page is darker again and counts 11 of 14 against 9); each other note's pre-stress and slide, and Eb3's slide, are set for equal temperament, not for the recordings; and every note is too dark against its recording, more plainly now that the unmeasured 12 kPa attack is gone. A tenor trombone on Braden's (2006) 14-element Conn 88H template (a population stand-in, no F attachment), whose pitch is never an input: the note is the lock between lip and bore. The pages carry per-note slide settings, a flow-noise row (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, an extrapolation) and a row that widens the lip opening as the lips part (q per note: 1.6 on F3, measured on one trombonist by Bromage, Campbell and Gilbert (2010), and none on Bb2 and Eb3 since 2026-11-10 (their earlier pages carried the measured 1.3 on Bb2 and the interpolated 1.514 on Eb3); 1.275 to 1.75 on G2, C3, Gb3, Bb3 and B3, interpolated between their four measured notes; and 1.4 on Ab4, above their top note, still the one number solved on Bb3 from Copley and Strong's printed areas, so borrowed; the q values partly stand in for lip swing the model lacks). Every page carries a uniform breath state in the bore (the steady full-breath bound, borrowed from woodwind sources), which raises the held note by 3.4 to 10.8 cents; the main slide is lengthened by 0.62058 % of the tube on Bb2, C3, Eb3, F3, Gb3, B3 and Ab4 (one rule from the two sound speeds, set against no recording), which gives the dry-air pitch back to within 0.7 cents; G2 keeps its slide because its page fell by one row on the count; Bb3's slide was reset by 31 mm before that rule existed, and its page also carries the exterior gas's absorption along the path to the microphone. The graded sound is the radiated pressure of the flanged bell, 1.524 m on axis, rendered at 19.2 kHz. Since 2026-11-10 B3 plays an earlier render under the best-count rule: the 2026-11-04 render (embouchure 19, the tube 40.7 mm shorter than the template, q 1.4, flow noise, the flanged modal bell, 6.22 kPa from the start with a 50 ms rise; it has no breath bore, no slide lengthening, no exterior-gas row and no q of 1.75). Bb2 plays a new render (2026-11-10): the card of its 2026-11-08 render (the breath bore with the 0.62058 % lengthening, the exterior-gas row, the flanged modal bell) with the lip rows and the blowing pressure replaced as the Bb2 entry of physics_present says. Eb3 plays a new render (2026-11-10) built the same way on the card of its 2026-11-08 render (the tuning slide pulled 84 mm in third position, the breath bore with the 0.62058 % lengthening, the exterior-gas row, the flow-noise row, the flanged modal bell), with the lip rows, the pre-stress and the blowing pressure replaced as the Eb3 entry says. The statements above about B3's breath bore, slide and q 1.75 describe the later B3 page, which stays in the page's history; Newton's human lip resonances are played on F3 and Bb1 only, and Bb2's lip carries Newton's Q and second mode but not Newton's 56.5 Hz; Eb3's lip carries a Q, a second mode and a lip opening interpolated between the Bb2 and F3 values of Newton and Bromage, and a resonance that is a setting.
physics_present: fs-couple brass_loop: a one-degree-of-freedom outward-striking lip island advanced by exact held-force propagation, a Bernoulli aperture solved implicitly with the mouthpiece cup junction, closing on the bore's reflectance
fs-duct multimodal transfer-matrix bore with exact Bessel viscothermal loss, realized as a passive causal line; the bell as Bessel horns expanded into cones lying exactly on their curves

full flanged modal radiation load at the bell, with the listener a finite-distance Rayleigh integral over every mouth mode, 1.524 m on axis, so the graded sound is radiated pressure and not mouthpiece pressure

the lip as printed by Cullen (2000, Table A.2): embouchure 7 on most pages, embouchure 19 on B3 and Ab4 (response measured, rest gap and width estimated by the thesis); pre-stress is a gesture, set per note (the Eb3 page called its 0.58 a player's setting until 2026-11-10 and now has 1.0); on F3 pre-stress is 1.0, the width is Copley and Strong's printed forte peak (13.4 mm) and only the mass and rest gap are Cullen's; the Bb2 and Eb3 lips are the ones the Bb2 and Eb3 entries describe (width 12 mm, Cullen's)

slide settings per note, stated on each page: the printed 4th position (G2), third position with the tuning slide pulled 84 mm (Eb3), and tuning-slide or tube-length changes on the others (Bb3: pulled 45.0 mm, then 31 mm more with its breath bore, 76 mm in all); with the breath bore the main slide is also lengthened by 0.62058 % of the tube, DL = L x (345.36 / 343.23 - 1), on Bb2 (16.9 mm), C3 (16.9), Eb3 (19.2), F3 (17.1), Gb3 (17.1), B3 (16.6) and Ab4 (17.1)

flow noise at the mouthpiece from the printed constriction law (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, as reprinted by Guedel 2005): a pressure source in each third octave, sized by the pressure across the lips at that instant and the card's own cup radius; no level was set against a recording

an area-height row: opening = width x height x (height / rest height)^(q - 1), q per note, from Bromage, Campbell and Gilbert (2010, preprint hal-00474644v1, Table 2: one trombonist, mezzo forte, high-speed video of the lips with a graph-paper calibration; q = 1.2 at Bb1, 1.3 at Bb2, 1.6 at F3 and 1.9 at F4, each for lip heights above 0.6 mm; over all notes and levels the same player's q runs from 0.95 to 2.4). q is measured on F3 (1.6) and was on Bb2 (1.3) until 2026-11-10, when the Bb2 page dropped the row, and is interpolated linearly in log2 frequency between the four measured notes on G2 (1.275), C3 (1.386), Gb3 (1.625), Bb3 (1.725) and B3 (1.75) (and was on Eb3, 1.514, until 2026-11-10, when the Eb3 page dropped the row), and stays 1.4 on Ab4, above the top measured note: that 1.4 was solved on Bb3 from Copley and Strong's (1996) printed areas and is borrowed. The form and its normalisation at each lip's own rest height are this model's own, and the same paper prints 1.49 and 1.55 at E3 for an artificial mouth. Against the pages that carried 1.4 the held note moved by -0.43 cents on Bb2, +0.40 on F3, -1.01 on G2, -0.98 on C3, +0.31 on Eb3, +6.28 on Gb3, +0.88 on Bb3 and +7.08 on B3, and the grader's count by +1 row on Bb2, Eb3 and Bb3, none on F3, G2, C3 and Gb3, and -2 rows on B3 (its short-time spectrum and fundamental frequency left their rulers); B3 and Gb3 were the brightest changes (B3 up by 12 to 13 dB at 2 to 4 kHz)

a uniform breath state in Bb3's bore, cup and lip, the steady full-breath bound and not a played-in state: 27 C, saturated, 4.5 % CO2 and 16.5 % O2 of the dry gas, borrowed from the clarinet and oboe cards' woodwind sources (Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969), with the room, the bell's load and the listener dry 20 C air. Without a reset the same bore sounded 15 cents above equal temperament (an unposted render) where the dry page sounds 6, so the player's slide is reset by 31 mm and the note sits on pitch (233.10 Hz, +0.1 c). Boutin, Smith and Wolfe (2020) filled a trombone with 26.3 C, 55 % RH lab air and measured the mean of impedance peaks 3 to 7 falling to about -0.60 % after 10 s, a band of about -0.5 to -0.7 % (read off their Fig. 4a, not printed values), and recovering toward and past 0 by 240 s; the same uniform breath bore in that lab air moves peaks 3 to 7 by -0.71 % in passive-bore scans of the card, at the lower edge of their band, and cannot show their recovery

the same uniform breath state in the bore, cup and lip of G2, Bb2, C3, Eb3, F3, Gb3, B3 and Ab4 (a row bore_gas on each page's V1 modal_baffle card): it moves the held note by +10.80, +10.05, +4.62, +10.72, +10.42, +3.41, +4.19 and +5.37 cents, that is 100, 93, 43, 99, 96, 32, 39 and 50 % of the bore's own +10.8 cents; the 0.62058 % slide lengthening above returns seven of them to the dry-air pitch within 0.7 cents (G2's page does not post: it falls from 10 to 9 of 14 on a single row)

on Bb3, the exterior gas's classical Stokes-Kirchhoff absorption and dispersion along every signed mouth-mode path from the bell to the microphone (a row observer_gas, commit 6ea217153): a tie at 12 of 14, the held note unchanged at 233.0974 Hz and at most 0.016 dB of change in any band above 1 kHz over 1.524 m of dry 20 C air; no humid-air relaxation law is declared

one blowing pressure from the start with a 50 ms rise and no attack: 6 kPa on G2, C3, F3 and Gb3, 1329 Pa on Bb2 and 1728 Pa on Eb3 (the measured mezzoforte medians), 6.22 kPa on B3, 7.132 kPa on Bb3 and 12 kPa on Ab4

on F3, and in trials on Bb2 (not on its page since 2026-11-10, which keeps Newton's Q and second mode but sets the resonance to 78 Hz, see the Bb2 entry; and in part on the Eb3 page since 2026-11-10, which interpolates Q, the second mode and the lip opening between the Bb2 and F3 values and sets the resonance to 99 Hz, see the Eb3 entry), the lip's two resonances as a human lip measured them: Newton (2009, PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh, section 4.4.2, the trombonist TJ; mechanical response by high-speed video with the lips driven by a loudspeaker sweep and little or no player overpressure, not under the flow of a played note): first mode 56.5 Hz with Q 2.0 on Bb2 (midpoints of the printed ranges 55 to 58 Hz and 1.6 to 2.4) and 100 Hz with Q 1.7 on F3 (printed as approximately 100 Hz and about 1.7), second, inward-striking mode (lip_response_mode2) 169.0 Hz with Q 3.9 on Bb2 (midpoints of 165 to 173 Hz and 2.8 to 5) and 200.0 Hz with Q 4.5 on F3 (around 200 Hz, midpoint of 4 to 5), k = m (2 pi fL)^2 and r = m 2 pi fL / Q with Cullen's artificial-lip mass, width and rest gap (borrowed: the thesis prints no human lip mass, width or rest gap), pre-stress 1.0 and nothing else changed; F3 sounds at 170.05 Hz, 46 cents flat of its equal-tempered note and the 170 Hz at which the thesis's player played this embouchure, and rises from 8 to 9 of 14; Bb2 does not sound its note but a harmonic series on 64.89 Hz, its lip opening to 9.0 mm against Copley and Strong's printed forte peak of 4.5 mm, and falls from 11 to 3 of 14; then with the lip width set to Copley and Strong's (1996, Table AI) printed forte peak lip-opening widths of one trombonist, read from the table's page image as slit widths (13.5 mm on Bb2, 13.4 mm on F3, in place of Cullen's 12 mm, and nothing else changed), Bb2 stays on a harmonic series, now 65.26 Hz, its lip opening to 9.44 mm, still 3 of 14, and F3 sounds 169.91 Hz, its lip opening to 2.93 mm, and rises from 9 to 10 of 14; the lip's DC opening is x0 = dp (1/mu) / (2 pi fL)^2, in which the face area cancels, so the opening scales with the borrowed 1/mu and the low printed human resonances drive it; on the F3 page now playing (6 kPa, lip resonance 100 Hz, Cullen's 1/mu of 0.063 m2/kg, second mode at 200 Hz with the borrowed 1/mu2 of minus 0.073 m2/kg) the outward mode's static displacement is 0.957 mm (dp x 1/mu / (2 pi 100 Hz)^2) and the second mode's inward displacement at rest is 0.277 mm (dp x 0.073 / (2 pi 200 Hz)^2), so no printed h0 enters that row and the lip opening quoted for that page is the one read from its render

a Bb1 page, the first of its slot (the pedal note, the first-position bore, a tenor trombonist's recording from Wikimedia Commons beside it under CC BY-SA 4.0), carrying the lip of a human embouchure for the pedal Bb1 as Newton, Campbell and Gilbert (2008, JASA 123(1), page EL18) measured it: resonances 32 Hz and 74 Hz as printed, Q 1.5 and 2.25 the midpoints of printed ranges (the second range from Newton 2009, another document), Cullen's mass, width and rest gap (borrowed), pre-stress 1.0 and q 1.2; its lip oscillates, at 51.12 Hz, 226 cents under Bb1, and opens to 20.8 mm against Copley and Strong's printed forte peak of 4.5 mm, so the page does not sound its note; an earlier render with the thesis set (38 Hz, Q 1.8, no second mode) did not oscillate at all; the grader has no ruler for a new slot, so it gives gaps and no count

the Bb2 page of 2026-11-10, the first page whose blowing pressure and lip rows come from prints (the card of the 2026-11-08 render with the lip rows and the blow replaced). What got worse against the page it replaces: the sound is darker (spectral centroid 330 Hz against 466 Hz, the recording's 641 Hz; centroid gap 6.65 to 11.79 semitones), spectral distance gap 7.21 to 14.75 dB, harmonic levels gap 3.81 to 11.88 dB, band envelope gap 6.12 to 8.75 dB, partial trajectories gap 12.90 to 13.63 dB, partial frequencies gap 0.11 to 0.13 cents, and the summed gap over the rulers rises from 9.67 to 10.37; the count rises from 11 to 12 of 14 (strict 11 to 12: short-time spectrum and spectral flux enter their rulers, the centroid leaves). The rows, each by origin: blowing pressure 1329 Pa, MEASURED (the median sustained mezzoforte mouth pressure of Bb2 over 385 notes of the 31 DigiMouth trombonists), against the 6 kPa of the earlier page, 4.5 times it; Q 2.0 and a second, inward-striking resonance at 169 Hz with Q 3.9, PRINTED midpoints of the ranges Newton (2009, section 4.4.2) prints for one trombonist's Bb2 embouchure (Q 1.6 to 2.4; 165 to 173 Hz and Q 2.8 to 5); 1/mu 0.15362 m2/kg (6.51 kg/m2), DERIVED from a print: 1/mu = h0 (2 pi fL)^2 / dp with h0 = 0.85 mm, the time-averaged lip separation of five trombonists at mezzo forte read off Bromage (2007, Fig 4.11), at the resonance used and the measured pressure; lip resonance 78 Hz, a SETTING chosen from the pitch of renders and never from the recording, which contradicts Newton's printed 55 to 58 Hz for the same embouchure (with that value the lip starts on a series of 63 to 65 Hz, an octave under the note; four values, 94, 86, 78 and 70 Hz, were rendered with the mass re-derived at each and 78 Hz was nearest the note by pitch before any grading: plus 22, plus 7, minus 1 and minus 8 cents); rest gap 1e-6 m, an ASSUMPTION (no rest opening of a player is printed in Bromage 2007, Newton 2009, Stevenson 2009 or Boutin and others 2020; the gap that reproduces Stevenson's printed onset of about 2.5 kPa belongs to a lip of another resonance and does not carry here); the second mode's 1/mu of minus 0.073 m2/kg and the 12 mm channel width BORROWED from Cullen's (2000) artificial lips; no flow-area row (the aperture is the plain width times the gap); a linear bore, so no wave steepening (the nonlinear-bore row is off). Against the players: the mean lip opening is 0.83 mm against h0 0.85 mm, the alternating mouthpiece pressure 1796 Pa rms against 1955 Pa measured at mezzo forte on Bb2 (the earlier page 8581 Pa, 4.4 times), the lip closed for 47 percent of the chunks (the earlier page 51), the lowest strong line 116.50 Hz, minus 1 cent, the grader's fundamental frequency gap 2.49 cents. The earlier Bb2 page's count, 11 of 14 (strict 11, summed gap 9.67), is the best this page has had; the stored 12 of 12 reading of version 20261110T072304Z is the grade of a clip cut twice and is not counted; the second mode pulls the lip inward at rest by 0.086 mm (dp x 0.073 / (2 pi 169 Hz)^2 at 1329 Pa), so the net static opening of this page's lip is 0.90 x h0 (0.764 mm), not h0, and the mean opening quoted above, 0.83 mm, is the one measured in the render

the Eb3 page of 2026-11-10, built the way the Bb2 page of the same day is (the card of the 2026-11-08 render with the lip rows, the pre-stress and the blow replaced). What got worse against the page it replaces: the sound is darker again (spectral centroid 342 Hz against 381 Hz, the recording's 671 Hz; centroid gap 10.13 to 11.97 semitones), harmonics-to-noise ratio gap 1.05 to 5.06 dB, cepstral envelope gap 11.66 to 13.50 dB, partial trajectories gap 11.60 to 12.89 dB, odd-to-even ratio gap 3.86 to 4.72 dB, spectral flux gap 0.88 to 0.90 dB, partial frequencies gap 0.41 to 0.42 cents; the summed gap over the rulers falls from 11.61 to 11.50; the count rises from 9 to 11 of 14 (strict 9 to 11: the scalogram and the attack enter their rulers, nothing leaves). The rows, each by origin: blowing pressure 1728 Pa, MEASURED (the median sustained mezzoforte mouth pressure of Eb3 over 242 notes of the 31 DigiMouth trombonists), against the 6 kPa of the earlier page, 3.5 times it; Q 1.786, a second, inward-striking resonance at 191.1 Hz with Q 4.329 and a lip opening h0 of 0.771 mm, INTERPOLATED and never extrapolated, linearly in log2 of the note's frequency, 0.714 of the way from Bb2 to F3, between the values Newton (2009, section 4.4.2) prints for one trombonist's Bb2 and F3 embouchures (Q 1.6 to 2.4 and about 1.7; second resonance 165 to 173 Hz with Q 2.8 to 5 and around 200 Hz with Q 4 to 5; the midpoints are used) and the mean lip separation of five trombonists at mezzo forte read off Bromage (2007, Fig 4.11: 0.85 mm on Bb2, 0.74 mm on F3); 1/mu 0.17274 m2/kg (5.79 kg/m2), DERIVED from a print: 1/mu = h0 (2 pi fL)^2 / dp with the interpolated h0, at the resonance used and the measured pressure; lip resonance 99 Hz, a SETTING chosen from the pitch of renders and never from the recording (six values, 99, 104, 109, 114, 119 and 124 Hz, were rendered with the mass re-derived at each, and 99 Hz was nearest the note by pitch before any grading: plus 0.2, 3.8, 7.8, 12.4, 18.3 and 26.1 cents; 99 Hz is the lowest value rendered, so none below it was tried); Newton prints no resonance for an Eb3 embouchure, and the 56.5 Hz printed for Bb2 and the about 100 Hz printed for F3 interpolate the same way to about 88 Hz, 11 Hz under the setting; the earlier page's effective resonance was 118.6 Hz (Cullen's 204.5 Hz times a pre-stress of 0.58); rest gap 1e-6 m, an ASSUMPTION (no rest opening of a player is printed in Bromage 2007, Newton 2009, Stevenson 2009 or Boutin and others 2020; the earlier page had Cullen's 0.53 mm); the second mode's 1/mu of minus 0.073 m2/kg and the 12 mm channel width BORROWED from Cullen's (2000) artificial lips; pre-stress 1.0 (the second mode runs only there); no flow-area row (the aperture is the plain width times the gap; the earlier page carried the interpolated 1.514); a linear bore, so no wave steepening (the nonlinear-bore row is off). Against the players: the mean lip opening is 0.72 mm against h0 0.77 mm, the alternating mouthpiece pressure 2062 Pa rms against 2044 Pa measured at mezzo forte on Eb3 (median over 188 notes; the earlier page 7985 Pa, 3.9 times), the lip closed for 43 percent of the chunks (the earlier page 41), the refined lowest line 155.58 Hz, plus 0.2 cents (the earlier page plus 4.9), the grader's fundamental frequency gap 0.99 cents. The best count this slot had before is 9 of 14 (strict 9), reached by three pages: Eb3-q1.4 (rendered 2026-11-04T19:22:00Z, summed gap 11.26), Eb3-cnoise (2026-11-04T17:10:48Z, 11.32) and the page replaced here (2026-11-08T07:21:05Z, 11.61); the second mode pulls the lip inward at rest by 0.0875 mm (dp x 0.073 / (2 pi 191.1 Hz)^2 at 1728 Pa), so the net static opening of this page's lip is 0.89 x h0 (0.684 mm), not h0, and the mean opening quoted above, 0.72 mm, is the one measured in the render
physics_missing: a player's lips: the lip is Cullen's artificial latex pair, outward-striking mode only on six of the nine pages, while F3 carries a human lip's printed resonances and Q on Cullen's mass, both modes, and Bb2 carries Newton's printed Q and second mode with a mass derived from a printed lip opening, and Eb3 the same interpolated between the Bb2 and F3 values (see physics_present), and Bb1, F2, Bb2 and F3 are the only embouchures of Newton's Figure 4.14; human outward resonances are far lower and more heavily damped, and no measured human lip mass is published, nor a lip width beyond Copley and Strong's forte peaks of one trombonist, now used on F3 (Newton's 2009 thesis, Table 4.2, prints human outward resonances of 32 to 60 Hz with Q 1.5 to 2.4 and inward ones of 70 to 100 Hz with Q 1.2 to 5, but no mass; Newton, Campbell and Gilbert's printed human Q of 1.2 and 1.8, put on the artificial lip with Bromage's rest gap 0.8 mm and q 1.3 and nothing else changed, does not start a note on Bb2, the lip never oscillating at 6 kPa)

the lip's swing: against Copley and Strong's printed heights (read on the pages that carried q = 1.4, and not read again on the per-note pages) this model's lip swings too far at the bottom of the range and too little in the middle, so the q values partly stand in for swing and should not be read as the lips' area law; fitting the print's own table gives about 1.1 to 1.2 for Copley and Strong's player, while Bromage, Campbell and Gilbert's player at mezzo forte runs from 1.2 (Bb1) to 1.9 (F4), so two trombonists' area laws differ and one player's four notes are all that set q here; the lips stay closed a larger share of the cycle than the print's 10 to 15 %

a second, inward-striking lip mode on the pages: the row is landed (lip_response_mode2, ae66a7c66), runs only at lip tension 1.0, which on this family was Bb3 (embouchure 7) and B3 (embouchure 19) until Bb2 and F3 took Newton's measured human embouchures at pre-stress 1.0, and only those two pages use it (see physics_present). With Cullen's printed second mode (Table A.2) at q = 1.4, a trial made when every page carried q = 1.4, it plays Bb3 38 cents flat and B3 19 cents flat, brightens both (band energy above 1 kHz up by as much as 14 dB; spectral distance 20.2 to 13.6 dB on Bb3 and 14.6 to 7.6 dB on B3) and costs rows, Bb3 9 of 14 against 12 and B3 9 of 14 against 10, so neither posts. At q = 1 it gave Bb3 11 of 14, and on Eb3 it played the wrong note in both forms tried (211.9 Hz and 138.6 Hz), so the family stays on one lip mode

the recorded trombone: the Iowa page gives no model, so the Conn 88H template is a population stand-in and the F attachment is absent; its mouthpiece and leadpipe (element 1) are digitized from Braden's Figure 5.3, not a measured table

a printed playing pressure: Copley and Strong print none and Boutin et al. 2015 print 1.4 kPa for notes played mp, so each hold is chosen so the lip speaks (6 kPa on most pages, 12 kPa on Ab4, the measured 1329 Pa on Bb2 and 1728 Pa on Eb3 since 2026-11-10). Blowing pressure moves the top of the sound a long way on this model, so that unmeasured choice matters. A trombonist's pressure has since been measured and is lower than the pages': DigiMouth (Amann, Chatziioannou, Nicolay and Willmann; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18679877, CC BY 4.0) recorded the intraoral pressure upstream of the lips of 31 trombonists with a sensor mouthpiece; taking the median over the middle 60 % of each note, with the sensor's zero from the rest segments of each file, the medians over notes are 1329 Pa at Bb2, 1728 Pa at Eb3, 1837 Pa at F3 and 2519 Pa at Bb3 played mezzoforte (358 notes at Bb3), 1929 Pa at Bb3 played piano and 2750 Pa at Bb3 played forte (286 notes, quartiles 2094 and 3146 Pa). The pages blow 6 kPa on F3 and 7.132 kPa on Bb3, which is 3.3 and 2.8 times the mezzoforte medians (Bb2 blew 6 kPa, 4.5 times, and Eb3 blew 6 kPa, 3.5 times, until 2026-11-10; they now blow the measured 1329 Pa and 1728 Pa): the holds were set from a number computed for this model's lip, not from a trombonist's pressure (Bb3's 7.132 kPa is 6000 / 5664 x 6733 Pa, 6733 Pa being the small-signal threshold the render script computed for pre-stress 1.0 once the reflection moved to the junction's own sample; the others stand at 6 kPa above theirs). A probe at the measured forte median 2750 Pa on the Bb3 card, 12 s long, did not reach the page's note: its mouthpiece AC rms grew from 7.4 Pa at 0.6 s with an e-folding time of about 1.1 s, slowed after 6 s and stayed at 825 Pa from about 8 s to the end, against the 7666 Pa that the page reaches, half of it by 0.3 s, at 7.132 kPa; over 10 to 12 s the lip swings between 0.51 and 0.76 mm and never closes, the radiated level is 6.8 % of the page's (23 dB lower) and the held note reads 234.9 Hz against the page's 233.2 Hz. At the measured forte pressure this lip makes a small steady oscillation after about 8 s and not the page's note; the pages' blow buys the amplitude and a start inside a page of 4 s

a player's slide: C3 and B3 are set with a tube shorter than the template, which a real player does not do (the hand slide goes out), and the template's own slide setting is not known, so read them as notes brought to pitch and not as slide positions; the 0.62058 % lengthening that gives the breath bore's pitch back is one derived length from the two sound speeds, not a measured slide position

dark sound: every page reads too dark against its recording (centroid well under the recording's). The 12 kPa attack the pages used to carry had no source and was hiding part of this: from 1.0 s the held note hardly changed when it came off, but over 0.3 to 0.9 s H8 on B3 read -19 dB with the attack and -35 dB without. The flow noise is close to flat with frequency, which is not the recordings' shape; the row is an extrapolation from dampers and plates in a large duct at 10 to 25 m/s
a clock that reaches the bell's radiation ceiling: the render runs at 19.2 kHz and everything above the receiver's resolved band is unmodelled
the microphone: an on-axis listener only; the player's bell orientation, any microphone directivity and any room are not modelled

a played-in breath state: every page's breath bore is one uniform state with no profile along the bore (none is printed for a brass bore), no wall heat transfer and no condensation (Boutin et al. measured wall losses up about 4 % after 240 s); wall vibration, nonlinear propagation and shock formation at forte (the source of brassiness), mutes, and the slide's own acoustic leakage. The steady blowing flow through the mouthpiece throat (Mach about 0.03 at 0.5 l/s and 0.07 at 1.1 l/s) is not in the linear loop: a lossless fs-duct diagnostic on the Bb3 bore moves its resonances down by 0.1 to 0.3 cents at 0.5 l/s and by 0.3 to 1.1 cents at 1.1 l/s, and the change of damping was not computed
a same-specimen impedance pair, so the passive chain is checked only against published population data

a C3 page at the measured pressure: tried on 2026-11-10 with the route of the Bb2 and Eb3 pages and not found. The card of each render was the C3 page's card with the lip rows, the pre-stress and the blow replaced: blowing pressure 1509 Pa, MEASURED (the median sustained mezzoforte mouth pressure of C3 over 128 notes of the 31 DigiMouth trombonists); Q 1.914, a second resonance at 177.9 Hz with Q 4.071 and h0 0.819 mm INTERPOLATED, linearly in log2 of the note's frequency, 0.285 of the way from Bb2 to F3, between the values Newton (2009) and Bromage (2007) print; 1/mu DERIVED from h0 at each resonance rendered and the measured pressure; rest gap 1e-6 m ASSUMED; the 12 mm width and the second mode's 1/mu BORROWED from Cullen (2000); pre-stress 1.0; no flow-area row; a linear bore. Eleven lip resonances were rendered with the mass re-derived at each, 76, 81, 86, 91, 96, 101, 106, 111, 116, 121 and 126 Hz, and none sounds C3: the refined lowest strong line lies 205 to 124 cents flat from 76 to 101 Hz (116 to 122 Hz), 83 cents flat at 106 Hz, 46 cents flat at 111 Hz (127.4 Hz, the nearest value) and, from 116 Hz, on a series at 174.7 to 176.4 Hz, 501 to 518 cents sharp (about a fourth above C3); the nearest value is 35 cents outside the grader's fundamental-frequency ruler of 11.07 cents, and the grader refuses that clip as not the named note (the strongest spectral line of the clip is 173 Hz, the note's fundamental 130.8 Hz). No third set of values was rendered. C3 keeps its page (Cullen's lip, 6 kPa, pre-stress 0.6), which reads 12 of 15 inside the ruler (strict 11, summed gap 10.83), the best count this slot has had under the rule (the stored 13-row reading of C3-cnoise, 2026-11-04, carries the unmeasured 12 kPa attack and is not counted; the stored C3-q1.4-soft page of the same day reads 12 of 15, strict 11, with a summed gap of 10.69)

a trombone Ab4 page at the measured pressure: tried on 2026-11-10 with two sets of eight lip resonances and not found. Blowing pressure 4301 Pa, INTERPOLATED in log2 frequency between the MEASURED DigiMouth mezzoforte medians of F4 (3674 Pa over 148 notes) and Bb4 (4719 Pa over 38 notes), Ab4 being 3 of the 5 semitones between them; DigiMouth has no mezzoforte Ab4 note, and Ab4's own crescendo median (4015 Pa over 17 notes) and forte median (5132 Pa over 10 notes) lie either side of it. The lip rows are the NEAREST print's, because Ab4 lies above every note that is printed: Q 1.7 and the second mode at 200 Hz with Q 4.5 are F3's (Newton 2009, section 4.4.2), and h0 0.30 mm is D4's (Bromage 2007, Fig 4.11, the time-averaged lip separation at mezzo forte, read off the plot, plus or minus 0.05 mm); the rest gap 1e-6 m is an ASSUMPTION; the 9 mm width (Cullen's embouchure 19 estimate) and the second mode's 1/mu2 of minus 0.073 m2/kg are BORROWED; pre-stress 1.0; no flow-area row; and every arm is in the V2 form (dry air, no breath bore, the bell a baffled piston), which the nonlinear bore needs, with a linear bore. Eight lip resonances, 260 to 400 Hz in steps of 20 Hz, were rendered twice, the mass derived at each from the printed opening. The first set used 1/mu = h0 (2 pi fL)^2 / dp, which fixes the outward mode's static opening at h0 and does not count the static inward pull of the second mode, x2 = dp x 0.073 / (2 pi 200 Hz)^2 = 0.199 mm: the net static opening was 0.101 mm and no arm sounded (level minus 104 to minus 92 dBFS, mouthpiece pressure 1 to 4 Pa rms). The second set used 1/mu = (h0 + x2) (2 pi fL)^2 / dp, so that the net static opening is the printed h0: the lip opened 0.300 mm on every arm and no arm sounded (level minus 93 to minus 86 dBFS, mouthpiece pressure 2 to 9 Pa rms against about 3 kPa measured, rising with fL, the top value of 400 Hz being 0.96 of the note). All sixteen are silent at 4301 Pa. Whether 4301 Pa lies under this lip's start threshold was not measured, and no third set was rendered. Ab4 keeps its page (12 kPa, Cullen's embouchure 19, pre-stress 1.7), which reads 10 of 15 inside the ruler (strict 10, summed gap 13.55); three stored pages read the same count (Ab4-bore-gas, summed gap 12.97; Ab4-q1.4, 13.48; Ab4-bore-gas-slide, 13.55). The nonlinear bore at 12 kPa in the V2 form was rendered the same day (9 h 22 min) and reads 4 of 15, with a spectral centroid of 1452 Hz against the recording's 700 Hz and the page's 539 Hz: it is tried and not posted

an F3 page at the measured pressure: tried on 2026-11-10 with the route of the Bb2 and Eb3 pages and not posted. The card is the F3 human-lip card with blowing pressure 1837 Pa, MEASURED (the median sustained mezzoforte mouth pressure of F3 over 603 notes of the 31 DigiMouth trombonists), Q 1.7 and the second mode at 200 Hz with Q 4.5, PRINTED (Newton 2009, section 4.4.2, trombonist TJ, F3 embouchure), 1/mu DERIVED as h0 (2 pi fL)^2 / dp with h0 0.74 mm (Bromage 2007, Fig 4.11, five trombonists at mezzo forte), at each resonance; the rest gap 1e-6 m is an ASSUMPTION; the 13.4 mm width (Copley and Strong 1996) and the second mode's 1/mu2 of minus 0.073 m2/kg are BORROWED; no flow-area row; a linear bore. Five lip resonances were rendered, 106, 114, 122, 130 and 138 Hz, the mass re-derived at each; by pitch, before any grading, the held note was minus 11.9, minus 5.7, plus 0.4, plus 7.2 and plus 16.7 cents from F3, and 122 Hz (1/mu 0.23670 m2/kg) was nearest, with a fundamental-frequency gap of minus 3.81 cents, inside the ruler of 4.98. It reads 8 of 14 inside the ruler (strict 7) against the page playing now, 10 of 14 (strict 9), and the summed gap 14.60 against 24.05: the spectral centroid (398 Hz against 453 Hz on the page playing and 686 Hz recorded), the harmonics-to-noise ratio (37.7 dB against the recording's 30.2 dB) and the odd-to-even ratio leave their rulers, while the fundamental frequency, the short-time spectrum and the attack gaps shrink. It is not posted. The second mode pulls the lip inward at rest by 0.085 mm (dp x 0.073 / (2 pi 200 Hz)^2 at 1837 Pa), so the net static opening is 0.89 x h0, not h0; the mean opening of the render in the sustain, 0.735 mm against h0 0.74 mm, is the figure to read

the nonlinear bore on the pages blown at a measured pressure: tried on 2026-11-10 on Bb2 and F3, in the V2 form, and not posted; the page's own card cannot take it. The parser refuses the page's rows beside bore nonlinear: for the flanged modal load, 'modal_baffle requires a linear bore and termination flanged; no foreign exterior load is substituted', and for the 27 C saturated breath-state bore, 'bore_gas needs modal_baffle: its flanged exterior load names the room gas, whereas the analytic mouth loads would radiate into the bore gas'; this is an incompatibility of the source, not a choice of the card. The V2 form that the nonlinear bore accepts therefore differs from the pages, on both arms of each note, in four rows: dry thermochemical air in the bore and the room in place of the breath state, a baffled-piston bell and receiver in place of the flanged modal load and the finite-distance Rayleigh integral over every mouth mode, full scale 100 Pa, and 3.0 s. The nonlinear row is `bore nonlinear 0.0024 16 2 128 20 8000 1e-2` (2.4 mm cells, 16 mechanics steps per output sample, 2 gas steps per mechanics step, the Zwikker-Kosten wall memory on 128 poles), and each arm is beside a V2 linear control on the same binary. Bb2 (the 1329 Pa page card, lip resonance 78 Hz): the control reads 11 of 14 inside the ruler (strict 11, summed gap 12.24) against the page's 12 (strict 12, 10.37), so the four rows alone cost one row; the nonlinear clip (8 h 36 min against 11 min) lifts the spectral centroid from 326 to 384 Hz, the recorded one being 641 Hz, and shrinks the gaps of spectral distance (13.8 to 11.2 dB) and harmonic levels (10.8 to 8.43 dB), moves the held note 3.7 cents flatter (fundamental-frequency gap 12.5 to 16.3 cents, ruler 5.51) and reads 9 of 14 (strict 8, summed gap 12.84), the short-time spectrum, the cepstral envelope and the fundamental frequency leaving their rulers. F3 (the 1837 Pa fL 122 card): the control reads 7 of 14 (strict 6, summed gap 15.89) against the page's 10 (strict 9, 24.05); the nonlinear clip (8 h 59 min) lifts the centroid from 404 to 539 Hz, the recorded one being 686 Hz and the page's 453 Hz, shrinks the gap of the upper harmonics to the first by 7 dB, reads 10 of 14 (strict 8, summed gap 15.29) and leaves the fundamental-frequency gap at 15.4 cents (ruler 4.98): the loose count ties the page's, the strict count is one below it, and the pitch is not inside the ruler, so it is not posted. At Ab4, blown 12 kPa, the same bore overshoots the recording (see the Ab4 entry). Whether the nonlinear bore helps on the pages' own breath-state bore and flanged modal load is not known: the breath state as the ambient and a mouth_load row are card rows that the nonlinear bore may take, which makes a different card (the room takes the breath state too, and the load is the plane-mode equivalent of the flanged load), and a bore gas distinct from the room is a source change that has not been sized
